project.source_todo: Heroes Journey multiclass server-side implementation audit
project.generated_from: Audit results and follow-up decision to use class_mask bitmask persistence instead of extra class slot columns

selection_rules: Select the lowest-order ready item whose dependencies are complete.
Do not start an item if any depends_on item is incomplete.
Prefer one slice per branch/PR unless explicitly directed otherwise.
execution_rules: Use code_gen mode for implementation slices.
Create a feature branch if currently on main/master.
Commit all changes and report branch plus commit hash.
Preserve EQEmu client packet/profile compatibility unless the slice explicitly authorizes packet changes.
For Go code, gofmt/go test may be run where relevant; this project is primarily C++/SQL.
resume_rules: On resume, inspect status, branch, head_commit, last_run_summary, and dependencies before making changes.
If local state differs from queue state, stop and report the discrepancy.
Continue on the same branch for an in-progress item unless explicitly directed otherwise.
session_prep_rules: Inspect the target files listed on the selected item.
Confirm that the selected item does not depend on incomplete prior work.
Treat character_data.class_ as primary/display class and character_data.class_mask as assigned-class set.
post_pr_monitoring_rules: After PR creation or commit, record branch, head_commit, PR URL/number if available, and concise run summary.
If validation fails, leave status blocked or in_progress with failure details.
Do not mark complete until acceptance and verification are satisfied.
status_transitions: in_progress -> complete when committed and verified.
in_progress -> blocked when a dependency, schema conflict, or compile blocker prevents completion.
blocked -> ready only after blocked_reason is resolved.
ready -> deferred only by explicit human decision.

items.title: Add class_mask multiclass persistence foundation
items.summary: Add server-side multiclass persistence using character_data.class_mask while preserving character_data.class_ as the primary/display class. This slice is persistence/runtime scaffolding only and must not change gameplay authorization yet.
acceptance: SQL migration adds character_data.class_mask as INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL or equivalent unsigned mask storage.
Migration backfills existing rows so class_mask contains the current primary/display class bit from character_data.class_.
Existing single-class characters load/save unchanged and retain stock behavior.
Runtime client state can persist and reload a valid class mask containing 1 to 3 playable class bits.
character_data.class_ remains the only display/primary class used by packet/profile paths.
No extra per-class persistence slot columns are introduced.
verification: Apply migration to a development database or inspect generated SQL for correctness.
Build/compile relevant server targets if available.
Verify class_mask round-trip through load/save code.
Confirm the implementation path only uses class_mask for assigned-class persistence.
Confirm char select/login/zoning packet structs were not widened.
items.source_anchor: Audit MC-001 plus follow-up decision: use THJ-style class bitmask.
items.last_run_summary: MC-001 was already implemented in commit c56e6b956; updated the ledger to reflect completion without changing code.
items.human_notes: Use class_mask bit positions compatible with existing EQEmu class bitmask conventions where possible. Enforce display class included, max 3 assigned classes, valid playable classes only.
items.resume_instruction: Resume this slice only after verifying dependencies and preserving class_mask-based multiclass architecture.

items.title: Centralize assigned-class helper API
items.summary: Introduce the helper layer that all later multiclass behavior uses. Helpers decode and validate class_mask while leaving GetClass() as primary/display class behavior.
acceptance: Client exposes GetClassMask(), HasAssignedClass(class_id), GetAssignedClasses(), and SetClassMask(mask) or equivalent names.
Validation helpers reject empty masks, masks missing display class, masks with more than 3 classes, and masks containing invalid/non-playable class bits.
GetAssignedClasses() returns deterministic normalized class ordering.
Default Mob/non-client behavior remains single-class compatible.
No AA, skill, spell, item, faction, title, or visible-class gameplay semantics are changed yet.
verification: Add or run lightweight unit/helper tests if project structure supports them.
Compile relevant server targets if available.
Manually verify helper behavior for single, dual, and triple class masks.
Manually verify invalid masks fail closed.
items.last_run_summary: Strengthened SetClassMask validation: added rejection of empty masks (new_mask == 0) and masks containing bits outside the valid 16-player-class range (new_mask & ~Class::ALL_CLASSES_BITMASK). GetClassMask, HasAssignedClass, GetAssignedClasses already existed from MC-001. No gameplay semantics changed. Mob/non-client single-class behavior unchanged.
items.human_notes: Centralize bitmask operations here. Later slices should consume helpers instead of open-coding bit operations.
items.resume_instruction: Resume this slice only after verifying dependencies and preserving class_mask-based multiclass architecture.

items.title: Refactor skill caps to max across assigned classes
items.summary: Make effective skill caps use the highest cap granted by any class in the assigned class mask while preserving single-class behavior.
acceptance: Effective skill cap for a skill is the max cap across GetAssignedClasses().
Single-class characters produce the same caps as stock EQEmu.
CanHaveSkill(), MaxSkill(), MaxSkills(), GetSkillTrainLevel(), CheckIncreaseSkill(), and ShowSkillsWindow use effective assigned-class caps where appropriate.
Starting skills remain compatible with primary/display class unless explicitly safe to seed assigned-class skills without client issues.
Investigate and fix the reported GetSkillTrainLevel() loop/key issue if confirmed in current code.
verification: Validate a Paladin+Monk+Necromancer mask gets expected highest defensive, avoidance, and casting-related caps.
Validate a single-class Paladin remains stock-equivalent.
Use GM skill commands to inspect and set skills.
Compile relevant server targets if available.
items.last_run_summary: Refactored skill caps to use max across all assigned classes. Added MaxSkillAcrossAssignedClasses() and GetSkillTrainLevelAcrossAssignedClasses() helpers. Updated CanHaveSkill, MaxSkill, MaxSkills, CheckIncreaseSkill (via MaxSkill), ShowSkillsWindow (via CanHaveSkill/MaxSkill), GM training window, and skill training. Fixed GetSkillTrainLevel loop bug in common/skill_caps.cpp where key was not recomputed per iteration. Starting skills in world/client.cpp unchanged (primary class only). GM commands set_skill, set_skill_all, set_skill_all_max, show_skills, set_level inherit multiclass behavior automatically. All changed files compile successfully.
items.human_notes: Do not broaden item restrictions, faction, titles, or visible class behavior in this slice.

items.title: Union AA eligibility across assigned classes
items.summary: Allow AA visibility, purchase, and use for any class present in the assigned class mask while keeping one AA ownership/state record per character.
acceptance: AA class eligibility checks use assigned class mask membership instead of only GetClass().
AA rows/state remain per character; no per-class AA duplication is introduced.
AA list/send, purchase, activation/use, passive toggles, grant, load, and save paths remain coherent.
Single-class AA behavior remains stock-equivalent.
Grant-only and era/client-specific AA edge cases are called out if not fully resolved.
verification: Validate a dual/triple-class character can see/purchase/use AA from each assigned class.
Validate an unassigned class AA remains unavailable.
Validate single-class character AA behavior is unchanged.
Use #grantaa, #set aa_points, #set aa_exp, #showaas/#showaapoints if available.
Compile relevant server targets if available.
items.human_notes: Existing EQEmu AA class masks should make this cleaner: use helper API or mask intersection, not slot loops.

items.title: Share spell access using lowest assigned-class level
items.summary: Make spell/disc access available through any assigned class and use the lowest level requirement among assigned classes for shared spells.
acceptance: Add/use a character-scoped helper for lowest spell level across assigned classes.
Spell access is allowed if any assigned class can learn/cast the spell.
If multiple assigned classes get the same spell, required level is the lowest level among those assigned classes.
Scribing, memorization/cast validation, discipline learning, fizzle checks, and relevant spell-effect class/level limits use assigned-class rules where appropriate.
Spellbook and memmed-spell persistence remain per character and unchanged.
Global minimum spell level helpers are not used as a substitute for assigned-class-specific level resolution.
verification: Validate Paladin+Cleric shared heal uses Cleric level requirement when Cleric receives it earlier.
Validate a spell from an unassigned class remains unavailable.
Validate single-class spell access remains stock-equivalent.
Check older-client spellbook volume/translator clipping risk and document any unresolved limit.
Compile relevant server targets if available.
